## Summary

There is a high severity vulnerability in Traefik's Kubernetes Ingress NGINX provider when several Ingresses share a host configured for client certificate authentication with the `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-secret` annotation. Since v3.7.15 the client authentication applies to the whole host and the TLS handshake uses the settings of the first Ingress declaring it, but the `Ssl-Client-*` headers were still built from the annotations of each Ingress: an Ingress with `auth-tls-verify-client: on` sharing a host with an Ingress using `optional_no_ca` forwarded `Ssl-Client-Verify: SUCCESS`, together with the subject and issuer chosen by the client, for a certificate that was never verified, and an Ingress without its own `auth-tls-secret` or without `auth-tls-pass-certificate-to-upstream` had no middleware handling these headers, so the values sent by the client reached the backend. An unauthenticated remote client can therefore present a forged client identity to a backend that trusts the proxy's verification result. 

The issue was introduced in v3.7.15; earlier versions are not affected, and Traefik v2 is not affected since it does not include the Kubernetes Ingress NGINX provider.

## Patches

- https://github.com/traefik/traefik/releases/tag/v3.7.18
- https://github.com/traefik/traefik/releases/tag/v3.8.0-rc.2
